messages.author: 942db0a1b7a33bfc
messages.subject: second order of bias
parts:
Dear ctmm,

In this tutorial https://ecoisilva.github.io/AKDE_minireview/code/AKDE_R-tutorial.html, you talk about the Expected order of pHREML bias. I was wondering what this is and  why do you use this formula? Are there any scientific articles that recommend this method or where I can learn more about it? I tried to look for articles but I was not sure if they talk about the same thing.

Could you use it to determine whether or not to exclude animals because their home range estimate is off? Meaning they have very big confidence intervals and probably are not range resident?

Kind regards,
Zohralyn

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: second order of bias
parts:
Hi Zoharlyn,

The paper where this method is derived is here:

https://besjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/2041-210X.13270

The reason discussed there (with some references) is that the method (perturbatively) has the same order of bias as REML, which varies from second order to none, depending on the model structure.

Very large area estimates resulting from very large range crossing timescales is one way that you could classify non-residents.

Best,
Chris
